mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a recessionary demand shock that depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising >= 0.4pp (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate revenue and prompts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by > 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) during episodes of two consecutive months with INDPRO falling > 1% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average by > 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5% mean) during periods of three consecutive months with HOUST > 12-month MA by > 10% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 1% in the same month indicates a dual monetary inflationary pressure that erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA by > 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month MA by > 1% in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during months when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month MA by > 1% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coincident with a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 in the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration that reduces earnings and consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises >= 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls by > 50,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8% mean) during months when UNRATE rises >= 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls by > 50,000 (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: An annualized quarterly growth rate in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weak consumer demand that depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2%).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized < 1% for 2 consecutive quarters AND FEDFUNDS >= 2%
regime_hint: weak consumption and neutral-to-tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7% mean) during periods of two consecutive quarters with GDPC1 < 1% annualized and FEDFUNDS >= 2% (t-test p > 0.10).
